assets.prompt: Preserve the tiny seated robot and exact valley composition; add a small ivory robot kitten seen from behind immediately to its right, with pointed ears, curved segmented tail and amber back/ear/tail components.
Add the same small back-facing ivory robot kitten beside the tiny robot in the original complete portrait valley; preserve camera and all landscape geometry.

notes: Desktop and phone each use one complete plate and projection. There is no split sky extension.
Clouds, creek reflections and waterfall highlights animate through registered GPU texture displacement, under one gently moving camera.
Original hero-bg.mp4 supplies only upper crops (desktop y=0..400, phone x=360..920/y=0..300), masked to the sky. Its observer and equipment are never sampled.
Small JPEG robot plates provide matching fallback compositions; a cropped night-sky image handles unavailable video.
Weather is a deterministic aesthetic cycle, not a forecast. Browser-local time controls the six phases.
Wetness, stream runoff and waterfall flow retain separate response times. OS/user reduced motion and offscreen pause are respected.
Night vegetation has a separate warm emission/bloom pass, applied after night exposure and before fog/rain, with a static fallback.
Only the nearest 14% of the photographic plate receives a softly feathered breeze displacement. Distant meadow and slope vegetation, robot and kitten remain still.
Companion amber components are identified by their native color inside tiny registered component footprints. No silhouette mask or dark oval is applied.
Camera travel amplitude is retained, but the former speed is multiplied by .45, giving approximately 45–60s cycles.
